slot.brief: Ask which of several triatomic/polyatomic species is non-polar despite polar bonds due to symmetric geometry (dipole moment zero).

stem: Which molecule has polar bonds but zero net dipole moment because of its molecular geometry?

verdicts.working: CO₂ is linear, so its two polar C=O bond dipoles cancel. The other molecules have nonzero net dipole moments.

working:
$\text{CO}_2$ is linear and has two identical $\text{C} - \text{O}$ bond dipoles directed oppositely.
$\vec{\mu}_{\text{net}}=\vec{\mu}_{\text{C}-\text{O}}+(-\vec{\mu}_{\text{C}-\text{O}})=0$
$\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is bent; $\text{SO}_2$ is bent; $\text{HCN}$ is linear but has unlike terminal atoms. Each has a nonzero net dipole moment.
